messages.author: 97d82fedb7016adb
messages.subject: way of fixing parameters?
parts:
Hi!

I often tend to pack my model parameters into vectors like

vector[10] theta;

Now, sometimes I want to fix a subset of the parameters to fixed values. How could I achieve this? I mean I would like to have some special prior here which fixes a value to a certain value. I know I can use a normal with an almost 0 sd, but this does not sound to be a good idea efficiency wise - and I anyway really just want to fix the parameter. Suggestions? Rewriting my program would be an option, yes; but this is time-consuming and error-prone.

So a construct like

theta[2] ~ fixed_prior(3);

would do the job, but maybe there is a more clever way to do it. As I recall doing theta[2] = 3 in the model block is a no go for obvious reasons.

Best,
Sebastian

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] way of fixing parameters?
parts:
> On Jun 26, 2015, at 5:44 AM, Sebastian Weber <sdw....@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> Hi!
>
> I often tend to pack my model parameters into vectors like
>
> vector[10] theta;
>
> Now, sometimes I want to fix a subset of the parameters to fixed values. How could I achieve this?

Declare the variable ones as parameters, then define
a transformed parameter theta that sets some elements to
the free parameters and some elements to constants.

- Bob

messages.author: 97d82fedb7016adb
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] way of fixing parameters?
parts:
Thanks Bob. I just did this, but it seems to kill the performance of the program. I did something like:

transformed parameters {
  vector[Ptot] theta;

  {
    int pr;

    pr <- 1;
    for(p in 1:Ptot) {
      if(fixed_theta[p] == 1) {
theta[p] <- prior_theta_gmean[p];
      } else {
theta[p] <- theta_raw[pr];
pr <- pr + 1;
      }
    }


...
 }

...
}

In the parameters block I have theta_raw defined. Is the way I handle the assignment bad for autodiff performance? Any other way of doing it fast?

Note: fixed_theta is a 0 and 1 int-array which indicates (as data) which parameter to fix to the prior mean value.

Many thanks!

Best,
Sebastian

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] way of fixing parameters?
parts:
You want that pr <- pr + 1 outside of the conditional.
Otheriwse, you get an infinite loop.

I honestly don't know what happens to everyone's indentation
on sending their code to us. I hope people aren't actually
writing code that looks like the below in terms of indentation,
because these kinds of errors are much harder to catch if
the block structure isn't clear.

- Bob

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] way of fixing parameters?

OK, I see. I don't like pr or p for variables at all,
because there are already too many of them floating around
in probability theory. But lots of models use p.

I don't know what you're comparing to, but that code itself
isn't going to cause a major slowdown --- it'll just get compiled
to a fast loop in C++.

- Bob
